title: Set a three-point bend fixture to a 16:1 span and centre the specimen on it
instruction: Set the bend fixture for this 10 mm thick specimen: move the two support blocks so their rollers are 16 times its thickness apart, centred on the red centre line, then lay the specimen flat across the rollers, centred and square to them. Let go of everything.
context: Three-point bend (flexural) tests of plastics and composites (ASTM D790, ISO 178) are run every day by materials-testing technicians in moulding, compounding and composites quality labs. The support span is set to 16 times the specimen's depth (its thickness; 16 +- 1 times is allowed), symmetric about the loading nose, and has to be reset for every new thickness; the bar is then laid flat across the two rollers, square to them and centred so both ends overhang equally. A wrong or off-centre span, or an off-centre or skewed bar, invalidates the flexural strength and modulus. Here the fixture is still set for the last specimen, a 4 mm bar (64 mm span), so both supports have to be moved out before the 10 mm bar goes on. The testing machine and its loading nose are not modelled: the red line marks where the nose comes down.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A three-point bend fixture stands on the midline. (1) Fixture base: a dark grey steel plate, 90 mm (x) by 300 mm (y), 10 mm tall, fixed to the table, spanning x 26.5-35.5 cm and y -15.0 to +15.0 cm. (2) Centre line: a red painted line, 90 x 2 mm and 0.5 mm thick, across the base's top along x at y 0, where the loading nose comes down. (3) Scale: 28 white painted ticks, 2 mm wide and 0.5 mm thick, along the base's near edge (from x 26.6 cm), one every 10 mm from 10 to 140 mm either side of the centre line; each is 8 mm long, those at 50 and 100 mm 12 mm long. (4) Two support blocks, loose, 0.13 kg each: a blue anodised aluminium block, 50 mm (x) by 30 mm (y) and 25 mm tall, with a bright steel roller 10 mm in diameter and 50 mm long fixed along the middle of its top, along x (the roller's axis 28 mm and its top 33 mm above the block's underside). They stand on the base centred at x 31.0 cm, y +3.2 and -3.2 cm, rollers along x and 64 mm apart, as set for a 4 mm thick bar. (5) Mat: black rubber, 40 mm (x) by 240 mm (y), 3 mm thick, fixed to the table, centred at x 19.0 cm, y +23.0 cm. (6) Specimen, loose: a cream glass-fibre-filled nylon (PA66-GF30) bar, 210 mm long, 20 mm wide and 10 mm thick (its depth), 0.057 kg, lying flat on the mat with its length along y, centred at x 19.0 cm, y +23.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the poses of the specimen and both support blocks and from both grippers (in a real trial: a steel rule, a protractor and a top photo). 'Standing': a support block upright within 5 degrees, the middle of its underside within 2 mm of the base's top and inside the base's outline, its roller within 5 degrees of x seen from above. Span s: the distance along y between the middles of the two rollers' axes. Offset e: how far the point midway between the roller axes is from the red line (half the difference of the two rule readings from the line to each roller's axis). 'On the rollers': the specimen lies on one of its 20 x 210 mm faces (its 10 mm thickness within 5 degrees of vertical), within 10 degrees of square to each roller seen from above, one roller on each side of its middle, and at each roller its underside is within 2 mm of the roller's top, its whole 20 mm width is on the roller's 50 mm length and the roller is at least 5 mm in from the specimen's end. Specimen offset c: how far the specimen's middle is, along it, from the point midway between where it crosses the two rollers (half the difference of its two overhangs past the roller axes). Square: the larger of its two angles from square to a roller. 'At rest': no end of the specimen and no roller axis moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. 'Let go': each gripper's fingers at least 20 mm from the specimen and from both blocks (a gripper's fingers are taken as everything within reach of a pad's outer corner around the 38 mm stretch back from the point between its pad tips: half the finger gap plus 8 mm out, 13.5 mm across; 57 mm when fully open). Score 0 unless both blocks are standing, the specimen is on the rollers, everything is at rest and let go, and s is within 10 mm of 160 mm (16 +- 1 times the 10 mm depth, the ASTM D790 / ISO 178 tolerance) with e at most 8 mm. Then the span scores 0.5 if s is within 5 mm of 160 mm and e is at most 5 mm, otherwise 0.25; plus the specimen 0.5 if c is at most 5 mm and it is square within 3 degrees, otherwise 0.25 if c is at most 10 mm, otherwise 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0 (success, held 1 s). 0.25: the span within the standards' band but more than 5 mm off 160 mm or more than 5 mm off the line, the specimen resting more than 10 mm off centre; 0.5: the span set and the specimen more than 10 mm off centre, or both only within the wider limits; 0.75: one of the two within the tight limits and the other within the wider ones. Leaving the supports where they start (64 mm apart), a support tipped over, off the base or turned across, and the specimen still held, on its edge, crosswise, down on the base or resting on only one roller all score 0. Either face of the specimen may be up and either end may point either way.
fidelity: Rigid bodies with the simulator's default friction. The base, red line, scale ticks and mat are fixed boxes. Each support is one loose rigid body (a block and a roller that cannot turn), free on the base (a real fixture then locks it with a screw). The specimen is a rigid box: it does not bend. No testing machine, crosshead or loading nose is modelled. The scorer reads only the poses of the specimen and the supports and each gripper's position and opening, not contact forces.
reset_notes: Put the two support blocks back on the base centred at x 31.0 cm, y +3.2 and -3.2 cm, upright with their rollers along x (64 mm apart), and the specimen back on the black mat centred at x 19.0 cm, y +23.0 cm, lying flat with its length along y. Nothing is consumed; everything else is fixed.
